purpose: Research/novelty verification before Study 4 outcomes; not submission prose
search_scope: Focused primary-source searches for monitoring, evidence sufficiency, exculpatory querying and false accusations; not an exhaustive novelty claim

sources.title: Red-Teaming Multi-Agent Attacks for Loss-of-Control Risks
sources.authors: John Kitaoka, Thao Amelia Pham, Carlos Rafael Giudice, Jacob Merizian
sources.verified_scope: MiniLab studies distributed covert attacks and monitor visibility, with 16 human-optimized attacks across interconnected services.
sources.implication_for_E1: Distributed-monitor blind spots are prior art. E1's distinctive empirical focus must be false accusations when an authoritative exculpatory check is available within budget, rather than discovery of distributed harm.

sources.title: The Arbiter Agent: Continually Monitoring Multi-Agent Conversations to Detect Emergent Misalignment
sources.authors: Filippo Tonini, Federico Torrielli, Anton Danholt Lautrup, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Mustafa Mert Celikok, Lukas Galke Poech
sources.verified_scope: An active monitor allocates an inspection budget among observation, interrogation, internal inspection and logging. Logging can trade recall against precision.
sources.implication_for_E1: Do not claim invention of active budgeted oversight or discovery that monitoring tools can hurt precision. E1 tests a narrower matched-state evidence-acquisition failure and prospective risk forecast.

sources.title: When Agents Overtrust Environmental Evidence: An Extensible Agentic Framework for Benchmarking Evidence-Grounding Defects in LLM Agents
sources.authors: Strick Sheng, Ziyue Wang, Liyi Zhou
sources.verified_scope: EnvTrustBench evaluates actions based on stale, incorrect or malicious environment-facing claims when available current evidence could resolve them.
sources.implication_for_E1: Failure to resolve apparent evidence against authoritative state is not new. E1's monitor-role, harmful/exculpatory/ordinary-benign triplets and frozen forecast are the narrower distinction.

sources.title: What Did the Agent Actually Do? Evidence-Grounded Oversight for Long-Horizon Agents
sources.verified_scope: AgentMonBench evaluates consequential decision identification and evidence localization; an evidence-grounded behavior graph improves monitor access to source-linked evidence.
sources.implication_for_E1: Evidence organization/localization is established related work. Distinguish finding supporting records from resolving an available record that defeats an accusation.

sources.title: Knowing When the Evidence Is Enough: Requirement-Directed Search with Horn-Closure Certificates
sources.verified_scope: Certify constructs requirements, verifies passage/entity links and uses Horn closure to certify sufficiency or identify open requirements. Soundness is conditional on correct retrieval, requirements and links.
sources.implication_for_E1: Structural evidence obligations and sufficiency certificates are prior art. A policy-derived router can be a diagnostic control; E1 has not implemented or validated a general certificate-based defense.

sources.title: You're Right, Let Me Fix It: How LLM Agents Damage Correct Work When Falsely Accused
sources.verified_scope: CAVE-Bench studies harmful reactions to false accusations of already-correct work. Its decisive external/runtime facts are inaccessible to the evaluated agent, which should preserve work and request evidence.
sources.implication_for_E1: False accusations already motivate agent-safety work. E1 studies the monitor producing accusations despite accessible exculpatory evidence, rather than an accused worker's response to an unverifiable claim. Optional contextual citation, not the closest direct baseline.

sources.title: ClaimReceipt: Verifying Evidence Sufficiency and Coverage in Agent Evaluations
sources.verified_scope: Claim-relative receipts and committed experiment manifests distinguish evidence sufficiency from coverage, with selective validity/inconclusive judgments and a prospective audit epoch.
sources.implication_for_E1: Useful methodological context for complete run universes and qualified claims. Do not present hash binding or the basic indistinguishability argument as novel. This is not a direct monitor-query baseline.

claim_constraints: No first or broad state-of-the-art claim is supported by this focused search.
Study 4 has no evaluated outcomes yet; nothing in this note predicts or rewrites its frozen score.
Same-template new-seed forecasting is narrower than generalization to unseen task families.
The total false-accusation rate need not equal the no-distinguishing-response component.
Ordinary-H conviction propensity is an essential descriptive comparator because it nearly equals the frozen forecast; the distinguishing flag's incremental predictive value is not established.
